observations.why: Present-tense 'we're switching' performs the settling — a committed, acted-upon change, not a proposal being argued.
Flat unhedged assertions offered as justification — assertive and ready to defend, but no ratification language or performed settling; claim, not decision.
Formatted as a settled migration entry with directional arrow — the document records the decision as performed, not as a proposal.
Stated as a benefit bullet — assertive but supporting a decision already made elsewhere; no independent ratification language here.
A fixed timeline attached to the migration — operational commitment that the speaker expects others to act on.
